title: The Fourth Column of the Eulerian Triangle: ⟨n,3⟩ = 4ⁿ − (n+1)·3ⁿ + C(n+1,2)·2ⁿ − C(n+1,3)
description: A fully machine-checked closed form for the fourth column ⟨n,3⟩ of the Eulerian triangle, extending the parent's columns 0, 1, 2. Stated over ℤ cleared of its /6 to avoid division: 6·⟨n,3⟩ = 6·4ⁿ − 6·(n+1)·3ⁿ + 3·n·(n+1)·2ⁿ − (n−1)·n·(n+1), equivalently ⟨n,3⟩ = 4ⁿ − (n+1)·3ⁿ + C(n+1,2)·2ⁿ − C(n+1,3) (OEIS A000498) — the third nontrivial case of the inclusion–exclusion formula ⟨n,k⟩ = ∑_{i=0}^{k} (−1)ⁱ·C(n+1,i)·(k+1−i)ⁿ. The proof is an induction on n driven by the definitional single-step Eulerian recurrence ⟨n+1,3⟩ = 4·⟨n,3⟩ + (n−2)·⟨n,2⟩, feeding in the parent's eulerian_col_two; the only subtlety is the truncated ℕ subtraction (n−2), which is harmless because ⟨0,2⟩ = ⟨1,2⟩ = 0. Verified against rows ⟨3,3⟩=0, ⟨4,3⟩=1, ⟨5,3⟩=26. 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

meta.author: Eulerian numbers (Euler 1755; Worpitzky 1883); formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib

mathlibDependencies.description: The parent's third-column closed form 2·⟨n,2⟩ = 2·3ⁿ − (n+1)·2ⁿ⁺¹ + n·(n+1), fed into the column-three induction through the recurrence ⟨n+1,3⟩ = 4·⟨n,3⟩ + (n−2)·⟨n,2⟩.
The Eulerian number ⟨n,k⟩ defined by the triangle recurrence ⟨n+1,k+1⟩ = (k+2)·⟨n,k+1⟩ + (n−k)·⟨n,k⟩; its definitional unfolding at k=2 gives the column-three recurrence used here by rfl.

originalContributions: eulerian_col_three: the closed form 6·⟨n,3⟩ = 6·4ⁿ − 6·(n+1)·3ⁿ + 3·n·(n+1)·2ⁿ − (n−1)·n·(n+1) for the fourth column of the Eulerian triangle (OEIS A000498), the next case after the parent's columns 0–2 and the third nontrivial instance of the Eulerian inclusion–exclusion formula

The induction is closed by the definitional recurrence ⟨n+1,3⟩ = 4·⟨n,3⟩ + (n−2)·⟨n,2⟩ together with the parent's column-two formula; the truncated ℕ subtraction (n−2) is reconciled with (n−2 : ℤ) by case-splitting n ∈ {0,1,≥2}, where for n ∈ {0,1} the vanishing of ⟨n,2⟩ makes the contribution zero either way

sections.title: The Fourth Column ⟨n,3⟩
sections.summary: eulerian_col_three: 6·⟨n,3⟩ = 6·4ⁿ − 6·(n+1)·3ⁿ + 3·n·(n+1)·2ⁿ − (n−1)·n·(n+1). Induction on n: the base is definitional; the step uses the recurrence ⟨n+1,3⟩ = 4·⟨n,3⟩ + (n−2)·⟨n,2⟩ (rfl), the inductive hypothesis, and the parent's eulerian_col_two, with a three-way case split on n to handle the truncated (n−2 : ℕ).
